title: Why the Cardano Foundation Took the Leap with Veridian
description: When discussing the Cardano Foundation, one often focuses on technological upgrades, governance votes, or academic papers. However, the foundation has recently taken a very interesting and decisive step. Recently, it formally spun off the internally incubated, decentralised identity proof project, Veridian, into a separate, profit-seeking entity registered in Switzerland. Instead of following the usual venture capital investment method, they transferred the majority of shares of this newly registered entity to tokenized shareholdings through the blockchain. These attempts not only transformed Veridian into a fully independent, profitable entity but also provided a real-world platform for the community's long-standing CIP-0113 programmable token standard. title: Understanding Cardano Programmable Tokens
description: One of the most proud pillars of the Cardano ecosystem is its native asset mechanism, which elevates custom tokens to 'citizens.' These tokens are inherently tracked from the origin and experience transmission and security as seamlessly as ADA, which is essentially the same. However, this design was also a double-edged sword. Because native token transmissions bypass complex smart contract executions and are directly handled by the base asset rules, issuing them becomes significantly more complex.

title: SecondFi Asset Recovery Tool Official Launch
description: Recently, inquiries have been ongoing within the community regarding the progress of the SecondFi incident. Since the vulnerability was exposed in June, a series of emergency asset freezing, cryptanalytic counter-engineering forensics, cross-party security audits, and post-recovery compensation phases have been carried out. Before providing detailed guidance on the official launch of the asset recovery tool and specific actions for affected users, this article will first outline the core context and timeline of the entire incident. The incident's full story and key timeline will be clarified, detailing the vulnerability exposure and hacker's on-chain theft from the SecondFi wallet (a form that branched off from the initial Yoroi client lineage). The hacker exploited a defect in the random number generation process during the software's digital signature creation process.

description: A warning from below: Those who have confirmed Linux kernel vulnerability CVE-2026-98432 and run a Cardano stake pool will understand how easy it is to procrastinate after updating the kernel. On October 30, Intersect (Intersect) urgently requested the aforementioned task to the stake pool operators (SPO). The problem was in the Linux kernel that nodes were sitting on. From the perspective of a delegate, there is no direct risk to the ADA in the wallet. However, if the pool server shakes, the rewards might also be affected. Therefore, there are some checks a delegate can do. On October 30, Intersect shared the content from the weekly update #
